QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_76

question.text: A client buys 50 lots of USDINR options (lot size USD 1,000 each) paying a premium of Rs 0.50 per USD. Per the currency derivatives workbook, stamp duty on currency derivatives is charged at 0.0001% on the buyer, and option trades are valued at premium. What stamp duty is payable?

answer.text: Rs 0.75 (using the equity-options stamp-duty rate of 0.003% on premium)
Rs 0.05 (using the equity-futures stamp-duty rate of 0.002% on premium)
Rs 4.18 (applying 0.0001% to the USD-notional value converted at Rs 83.50)

explanation.text: The Logic: Premium value = 50 lots x USD 1,000 x Rs 0.50 = Rs 25,000. Stamp duty on currency derivatives is 0.0001% on the buyer, applied to the premium value for options: 0.0001% x Rs 25,000 = Rs 0.025. The Trap: 0.003% is the equity-options stamp-duty rate, not the currency-options rate. 0.002% applies to equity futures. Applying 0.0001% to the USD-notional value instead of the premium ignores the workbook rule that option stamp duty is computed on premium, not notional. Note: Stamp duty is collected centrally by the exchange / clearing corporation under the Indian Stamp Act post the 2020 amendments. Rates vary by segment: 0.0001% on the buyer for currency and interest-rate derivatives, 0.002% on the buyer for equity futures and 0.003% on the buyer for equity options.
